mainTopic: Whether the blood and fluids of non-Jews make impure, and the idea of a היכרא that shows an impurity is only rabbinic
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier story. The כהן גדול was not worried about the spit of a plain עם הארץ, because it was a רגל. On a רגל the רבנן treated every Jew as a חבר, based on a פסוק in שופטים. A new משנה then brings two disputes between בית שמאי and בית הלל. The first is about the blood of a נכרית and the דם טהרה of a מצורעת. The second is about the blood of a יולדת who has not yet immersed. It also gives a case where everyone agrees, a יולדת בזוב. The גמרא asks how בית שמאי can call a נכרית's blood pure when חז"ל decreed that גוים are like זבין. It explains that any decree on her blood would confuse people about the Torah rule, so her pure blood serves as a היכרא. רבא then rules that a נכרי man's זוב is impure even for בית שמאי, and his קרי is pure even for בית הלל, with the pure קרי acting as the sign. The גמרא tries to support רבא, first from a משנה, which is rejected, and then from a ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: It was a רגל, so an עם הארץ counted as pure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the incident happened on a רגל. At that time the רבנן treated the impurity of an עם הארץ as purity.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was a pilgrimage Festival, and the Rabbis treated the impurity of an עם הארץ during the Festival as if it were purity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering a question from just before this section. Why was the כהן גדול worried only that the spitter was a צדוקי, when the spit of any עם הארץ is impure? The answer is that it was a רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the saliva of an עם הארץ is treated as impure, because we suspect he is not careful about טומאה. On a רגל, though, the רבנן set aside this suspicion and treated him as pure. So the only real worry left was that this man was a צדוקי, whose wife might be a נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: A pilgrimage Festival (פסח, שבועות, סוכות)
An unlearned Jew who is not trusted to be careful about purity
Ritual impurity
They made it / treated it as

phrases.english: It was a pilgrimage Festival,
phrases.notes: This answers why the כהן גדול did not worry about the spit of an ordinary עם הארץ.

phrases.english: and the impurity of an am ha'aretz during the Festival
the Rabbis treated as purity,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised just before this section about why only a צדוקי was a concern.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Situational limitation: the event happened at a time when a special leniency applied
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any עם הארץ's spit should have worried the כהן גדול.
steps.terutzMaskana: On a רגל, an עם הארץ's impurity is treated as purity, so only the צדוקי concern remained.

steps.title: The פסוק calls all of Israel חברים when they gather
steps.stepSummary: The source for the רגל leniency is a פסוק that describes all of Israel gathering together as חברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And all the men of Israel gathered to the city, like one man, united (חברים).' The verse made all of them חברים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק as the source for the leniency it just stated about the רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word חברים in the פסוק is read as the technical term חבר, meaning someone trusted about purity. When all of Israel gathers in one place, like on a רגל, the פסוק gives every one of them that trusted status, even an עם הארץ.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'united'; read here as people trusted to keep the laws of purity
The verse made them (gave them a status)

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why on the רגלים we do not treat people's touch as impure, even though many of those gathered are not careful about טומאה.

phrases.english: as it is written:
"And all the men of Israel gathered
to the city, like one man, united,"
the verse made all of them chaverim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural basis for the leniency in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The רגל leniency that an עם הארץ's impurity counts as purity
steps.raayaSupportSource: שופטים 20:11, where all of Israel gathered are called חברים

steps.title: משנה: blood of a gentile woman and a leper's days of purity
steps.stepSummary: The משנה brings a מחלוקת. בית שמאי say the blood of a נכרית and the דם טהרה of a מצורעת is pure. בית הלל say it is like her רוק and מימי רגלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNAH: The blood of a gentile woman, and the blood of purity of a woman who is a מצורעת, בית שמאי declare pure. בית הלל say: it is like her saliva and her urine.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It deals with two kinds of blood that are not regular נדה blood and asks if they make anything impure at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי say these bloods are completely pure. בית הלל say they have the same status as the woman's spit and urine. That means they make impure only while still wet, not once they dry. So בית הלל are stricter than בית שמאי, but not as strict as real נדה blood.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה
A non-Jewish woman
Blood seen in the days after birth when a woman's blood is normally pure
A woman with צרעת
Like her saliva and her urine: impure only while wet

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read בית הלל as saying this blood is fully like נדה blood. 'Like her saliva and urine' means it makes impure only while it is moist, not after it dries.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
The blood of a gentile woman
and the blood of purity of a woman who is a leper,
phrases.notes: This means she gave birth and sees blood during the days when a new mother's blood is normally pure.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai declare them pure,
and Beit Hillel say:
It is like her saliva and her urine.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי' דַּם נׇכְרִית וְדַם טׇהֳרָה שֶׁל מְצוֹרַעַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה, separate from the story discussed above.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: pure. בית הלל: makes impure like her saliva and urine, only while moist.

steps.title: משנה: blood of a new mother who has not immersed
steps.stepSummary: Here the positions reverse in strictness. בית שמאי say the blood of a יולדת who did not go to the מקוה is like רוק and urine. בית הלל say it makes impure whether wet or dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: The blood of a woman who gave birth and did not immerse: בית שמאי say it is like her saliva and urine. בית הלל say it makes impure whether wet or dry.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second מחלוקת. It is about a woman whose days of impurity after birth are over but who has not yet gone to the מקוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי hold that once her days of impurity end, her blood is no longer like נדה blood, even before טבילה. So it is impure only while wet. בית הלל hold that since she has not yet immersed, the blood keeps its full impure status. That means it makes impure even when dry, just like נדה blood.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who gave birth
Immersed in a מקוה
Makes impure whether moist or dry

phrases.english: The blood of a woman who gave birth who did not immerse,
phrases.notes: Her days of impurity after the birth have already ended; she just hasn't gone to the מקוה yet.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:
It is like her saliva and her urine,
and Beit Hillel say:
It makes impure whether moist or dry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case in the same משנה, here with בית הלל taking the stricter view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: impure only while moist. בית הלל: impure whether moist or dry, because she has not immersed.

steps.title: בית שמאי agree about a woman who gave birth as a זבה
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי agree that a יולדת בזוב makes impure whether her blood is wet or dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they agree about a woman who gave birth while a זבה, that her blood makes impure whether moist or dry.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes by naming a case where there is no מחלוקת. בית שמאי agree with בית הלל's strict ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יולדת בזוב still has to count seven clean days after her days of impurity are over. Because she is still in that counting, even בית שמאי agree her blood is fully impure, wet or dry. This limits בית שמאי's leniency from step 4 to a regular יולדת.

keyTerms.meaning: They agree (here, בית שמאי agree with בית הלל)
A woman who gave birth while in a state of זיבה

steps.whatToRemember: In the first case (נכרית, מצורעת), בית שמאי say the blood is pure and בית הלל say it makes impure while wet. In the second case (a יולדת who has not immersed), בית שמאי say it makes impure only while wet and בית הלל say it makes impure wet or dry. For a יולדת בזוב, everyone agrees it makes impure wet or dry.

phrases.english: And they agree regarding a woman who gave birth as a zavah
that she makes impure whether moist or dry.
phrases.notes: 'They' here means בית שמאי, who agree with בית הלל in this case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits בית שמאי's leniency in step 4 by giving a case where they agree with בית הלל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees a יולדת בזוב's blood makes impure whether moist or dry.

steps.title: Don't בית שמאי accept the decree that גוים are like זבין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how בית שמאי can call a נכרית's blood pure, when there is a known decree that גוים are treated like זבין in every way.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Don't בית שמאי accept the teaching on the פסוק 'Speak to בני ישראל... any man who is a זב'? It teaches that בני ישראל become impure through זיבה and גוים do not, but חז"ל decreed that גוים should be like זבין in all their matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by attacking the view of בית שמאי in the משנה, who said the blood of a נכרית is pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, a גוי does not become a זב. But חז"ל made a decree that גוים are like זבין 'in all their matters.' If the decree covers everything, a נכרית's blood should also be impure, so how can בית שמאי call it pure?

keyTerms.meaning: A person with an impure bodily discharge, which makes him טמא
The impure discharge that makes someone a זב
Non-Jews
They (חז"ל) made a rabbinic decree

phrases.english: GEMARA: And do בית שמאי not hold
"Speak to the children of Israel
and say to them
any man who has a discharge [is a זב]"
the children of Israel become impure through זיבה,
but non-Jews do not become impure through זיבה;
but [the Sages] decreed about them
that they should be like זבין in all their matters?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of בית שמאי in the משנה (step 3) that a נכרית's blood is pure.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of בית שמאי that the blood of a נכרית is pure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The decree makes גוים like זבין in all matters, so it should include a נכרית's blood too.

steps.title: No good way to decree on a נכרית's blood
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי answer that a decree on her blood would either look exactly like Torah impurity or would wrongly split the Torah rule, so חז"ל did not decree on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי can tell you: (That decree was said about males, because if it were about females,) how would we do it? If her blood is impure whether wet or dry, you made it just like Torah impurity. If it is impure when wet but not when dry, you made a split in the Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי explain why the decree cannot apply to a נכרית's blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real Torah-level blood is impure both wet and dry. If the rabbinic decree copied that exactly, people could not tell rabbinic impurity from Torah impurity. If the decree made it impure only when wet, people might wrongly think Torah blood also stops being impure once it dries. So the safest choice was no decree on her blood at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Wet and dry
You made it like a Torah law
You split up a Torah law, making it look like it has different levels

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not that her blood should really be impure. The problem is that any version of a decree would confuse people about the Torah rule for Jewish women's blood.

phrases.english: בית שמאי can say to you:
(That was stated about males,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. Either way, the point is that the decree doesn't cover a woman's blood.

phrases.english: for if [it were] about females)
how should one act?
Should it make impure whether wet or dry?
Then you have made it like [impurity] of the Torah.
Should it make impure when wet and not make impure when dry?
Then you have made a split in [impurity] of the Torah.
phrases.notes: People seeing this might think Jewish women's blood also becomes pure once it dries.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the decree: it cannot practically apply to a woman's blood
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The decree that גוים are like זבין covers everything, including a נכרית's blood.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both possible ways of decreeing on her blood would confuse people about the Torah law, so her blood stays pure.

steps.title: Then her רוק and urine should also be pure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: by that logic, her רוק and urine should also be left pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, her רוק and urine too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer by applying the same reasoning to her רוק and urine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her רוק and urine are impure by rabbinic decree only when wet, which matches the Torah rule for a Jewish זבה. That looks just like Torah impurity, so the same worry of mixing up the two levels should apply. Why weren't they left pure too?

keyTerms.meaning: If so, a common way to say 'by your logic...'
Saliva
Urine

phrases.english: If so,
her saliva and her urine too [should be pure]!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, רוּקָּהּ וּמֵימֵי רַגְלֶיהָ נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning given in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The worry about making rabbinic impurity look like Torah impurity
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Her רוק and urine also look exactly like Torah impurity, yet they were decreed impure.

steps.title: The pure blood is the sign
steps.stepSummary: Since her blood is fully pure, that difference acts as a sign, and everyone will know her רוק and urine are only rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since we make a sign with her blood, it will be known that her רוק and urine are only rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that one clear difference is enough to prevent confusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving her blood fully pure shows that her impurity is not like a Jewish woman's. Once people see that difference, they understand that her רוק and urine are only impure מדרבנן. So there is no danger of mixing them up with Torah impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: A noticeable sign or marker that shows something is different
From the Sages (rabbinic), not from the Torah
It is clearly known

phrases.english: Since we make a marker with her blood,
it will surely be known
that her saliva and her urine are [impure] by rabbinic law.

steps.terutzResolutionType: One marker is enough to show the whole status is rabbinic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Her רוק and urine should also be pure to avoid confusion.
steps.terutzMaskana: The purity of her blood already shows her impurity is rabbinic, so her רוק and urine can stay impure.

steps.title: Why not make the sign with רוק and urine instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why חז"ל didn't do it the other way: leave her רוק and urine pure as the sign, and make her blood impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let them make the sign with her רוק and urine, and make her blood impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the choice of which item serves as the sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one sign is enough, it could just as well be her רוק and urine that are left pure. Then her blood could be impure even when dry, and people would still know it is only rabbinic. Why pick the blood as the sign?

keyTerms.meaning: And let them make / do
To make impure / declare impure

phrases.english: But let them make the marker
with her saliva and her urine,
and declare her blood impure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 9 by suggesting the reverse arrangement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of blood as the marker
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one marker is enough, the marker could be on רוק and urine, leaving her blood impure.

steps.title: Decrees are made on common things
steps.stepSummary: רוק and urine are common, so חז"ל decreed on them. Her blood is not common, so they did not decree on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Her רוק and urine, which are common, חז"ל decreed about. Her blood, which is not common, חז"ל did not decree about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final answer: חז"ל aimed the decree at what happens often.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A decree is most needed for things people meet all the time, like רוק and urine. Blood from a נכרית is not commonly found, so there was less need to decree. That is why the blood was the one left pure and used as the sign.

keyTerms.meaning: Common, happens often
Not common, rare

steps.whatToRemember: According to בית שמאי, a נכרית's blood is pure because any decree on it would blur the Torah rule. Her רוק and urine are still impure because they are common, and the pure blood already shows that her impurity is only rabbinic.

phrases.english: Her saliva and her urine, which are common,
the Sages decreed about them;
her blood, which is not common,
the Sages did not decree about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 and closes the discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical distinction based on how common each item is
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The marker could just as easily be placed on רוק and urine.
steps.terutzMaskana: חז"ל decreed on common items (רוק and urine) and not on the uncommon one (blood).

steps.title: רבא's ruling on a gentile man's discharge and semen
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a נכרי man's זוב is impure even for בית שמאי, and his קרי is pure even for בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A gentile man's זוב is impure even according to בית שמאי, and his semen is pure even according to בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא moves from the נכרית woman to a נכרי man and gives a two-part ruling. Each part holds even for the side you would least expect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the woman, בית שמאי left her blood fully pure, so you might think they would also leave his זוב pure, but רבא says no. בית הלל made her blood impure, so you might think they would make his קרי impure, but רבא says no.

keyTerms.meaning: An abnormal discharge from a man that normally makes him a זב
Semen, a seminal emission
Even according to: the ruling holds even for the side you would expect to disagree

steps.confusionAlert: Under Torah law a נכרי does not become impure at all. Everything here is a rabbinic decree, which is why the 'sign' idea matters so much.

phrases.english: Rava said:
His ziva is impure, even according to Beit Shammai;
phrases.notes: "His" means a gentile man. The גמרא has just finished talking about a gentile woman.

phrases.english: his semen is pure, even according to Beit Hillel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: זוֹבוֹ טָמֵא, אֲפִילּוּ לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the woman's logic about a 'sign' to a parallel case: the man's two fluids.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נכרי man's זוב is rabbinically impure according to everyone. His קרי is pure according to everyone.

steps.title: Why his discharge is impure even for בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: His זוב can be impure because his קרי, which stays pure, serves as the sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: His זוב is impure even according to בית שמאי, because a sign can be made with his semen.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the first half of his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי's worry in step 7 was that a decree would be confused with Torah impurity. That worry goes away here because his קרי stays pure, and that difference shows everyone his זוב impurity is only rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: A sign or marker that shows people a law is only rabbinic
To make or do

phrases.english: His ziva is impure, even according to Beit Shammai —
since it is possible to make a sign with his semen.
phrases.notes: Since his semen stays pure, people will see the difference and know his זוב is only impure מדרבנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the first half of רבא's ruling.

steps.title: Why his semen is pure even for בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: חז"ל left his קרי pure as a sign, so people won't burn תרומה and קדשים over his rabbinic impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: His semen is pure even according to בית הלל. חז"ל made it a sign so that people would not burn תרומה and קדשים because of it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the second half of his ruling: his קרי was purposely left pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even בית הלל need a sign. Otherwise people would treat the man's rabbinic impurity like Torah impurity and burn holy food it touched, which is only done for Torah-level impurity. Leaving his קרי pure provides that sign.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן, which is holy
Sacrificial or consecrated items
To burn: what is done to תרומה or קדשים that became impure by Torah law

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the practical danger of a rabbinic decree that looks like Torah law: people would destroy holy food for no real reason.

phrases.english: His semen is pure, even according to Beit Hillel —
the Rabbis made it a sign,
so that people will not burn because of it
phrases.notes: "It" means things touched by the gentile's זוב, which is only impure מדרבנן.

phrases.english: teruma and consecrated items.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the second half of רבא's ruling, using the same sign idea.

steps.title: Why not reverse it: discharge pure, semen impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why חז"ל didn't leave his זוב pure as the sign and make his קרי impure instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let חז"ל make the sign with his זוב, and make his semen impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the choice of which fluid stays pure. Either one could serve as the sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one fluid needs to stay pure for the sign to work. So why was קרי chosen and not זוב? This is the same kind of question as step 10 about the woman.

keyTerms.meaning: To declare impure
And let them make: a challenge offering another way it could have been done

phrases.english: But let them make the sign with his ziva,
and declare his semen impure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges which fluid חז"ל chose as the sign.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's choice of קרי, not זוב, as the fluid that stays pure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The sign works with either fluid, so the reverse arrangement seems equally possible.

steps.title: Discharge comes on its own; semen depends on an action
steps.stepSummary: חז"ל decreed on זוב because it does not depend on any action, but not on קרי, which does.
steps.simpleTranslation: His זוב, which does not depend on an action, חז"ל decreed impure. His semen, which depends on an action, חז"ל did not decree impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two fluids are different. זוב comes out by itself, while קרי comes from something the man does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding factor is whether the discharge depends on an action. זוב just happens, so חז"ל put a decree on it. קרי depends on his action, so they left it alone and it became the sign. This follows the pattern of step 11, where the choice of what to decree on was based on the nature of each fluid.

keyTerms.meaning: Depends on an action
They decreed: made a rabbinic enactment

steps.whatToRemember: For a נכרי man, his זוב is rabbinically impure and his קרי is pure according to both בית שמאי and בית הלל. The pure קרי is the sign that shows the impurity is only rabbinic. חז"ל chose זוב for the decree because it does not depend on an action.

phrases.english: His ziva, which does not depend on an action —
the Rabbis decreed on it;
his semen, which depends on an action —
the Rabbis did not decree on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹבוֹ דְּלָא תְּלֵי בְּמַעֲשֶׂה גְּזַרוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 by showing a real difference between the two fluids.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either fluid could equally serve as the sign, so the choice seems arbitrary.
steps.terutzMaskana: זוב comes without any action and so received the decree. קרי depends on an action, so it was left pure as the sign.

steps.title: A משנה seems to support רבא: semen from a נכרי is pure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a משנה, which calls semen from a נכרי 'pure,' supports רבא's view that it is fully pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports רבא? A gentile woman who discharged semen from a Jew: it is impure. A Jewish woman who discharged semen from a gentile: it is pure. Doesn't 'pure' mean completely pure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that might prove רבא right. The משנה says semen from a נכרי is 'pure,' and the גמרא suggests this means completely pure, even מדרבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What decides purity here is whose semen it is, not which woman discharged it. A Jew's semen is impure even inside a נכרית, and a נכרי's semen is pure even inside a בת ישראל. The proof depends on reading 'pure' as fully pure, with no rabbinic impurity at all, which is exactly רבא's claim from step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: supports him; a source that backs up an earlier opinion
who discharged, who expelled
'Doesn't it mean...?' The גמרא pushes a source toward one reading
completely pure, pure on every level

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבא, who said a נכרי's קרי is pure even for בית הלל (step 12). The source is a משנה in מקואות (8:4).

phrases.aramaic: נׇכְרִית שֶׁפָּלְטָה שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל — טְמֵאָה,
phrases.english: A gentile woman who discharged semen from a Jew: it is impure,
and a Jewish woman who discharged semen
from a gentile: it is pure.
Doesn't this mean completely pure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining why חז"ל left a נכרי's קרי pure, the גמרא looks for a source that supports רבא's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that a נכרי's semen is pure even מדרבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה (מקואות): a Jewish woman who discharged semen from a נכרי is pure

steps.title: Rejected: 'pure' may only mean pure by Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the משנה may mean pure מדאורייתא but still impure מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means pure by Torah law, but impure by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. The word 'pure' in the משנה could simply mean pure on the Torah level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees a נכרי's semen is pure מדאורייתא. The real question is whether חז"ל made it impure. Since the משנה may only be speaking about Torah law, it does not show that רבא is right about rabbinic law, so the proof fails.

keyTerms.meaning: by Torah law
by rabbinic law, a decree of חז"ל

steps.confusionAlert: This does not prove רבא wrong. It only shows the משנה does not prove him right. The משנה can be read either way.

phrases.english: No, pure by Torah law,
impure by rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה, not רבא's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'pure' can mean pure only מדאורייתא, so it does not prove the semen is free of rabbinic impurity.

steps.title: A second attempt: a ברייתא about a Jew's semen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא that may support רבא, starting with the rule that a Jew's semen is impure everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: You end up saying that a Jew's semen is impure wherever it is,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a second possible proof for רבא by starting to quote a ברייתא. The key part of the quote comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא opens by stating that a Jew's semen is impure no matter where it is found, even inside a נכרית. That matches the משנה above. The contrast with a נכרי's semen, which will decide whether this proves רבא's point, has not been said yet.

keyTerms.meaning: 'you end up saying,' a summing-up phrase
semen
in every place, wherever it is found

phrases.english: Come and hear:
You end up saying,
the semen of a Jew
is impure wherever it is,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, the גמרא begins a new source to try to support רבא.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that a נכרי's semen is pure even מדרבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא summing up the purity rules for semen (it continues past this section)
